key_impacts: Large-scale nuclear disaster caused ongoing harm to people in Japan.
Melting of nuclear fuel inside Fukushima Daiichi reactors occurred.
Coolant water became extremely contaminated and leaked into basements.
Vast volumes of contaminated water stored on-site in large tanks with toppling risk.
Continued cooling needed to avoid further release of radioactive materials.
evidence_snippets: Large-scale nuclear disaster at TEPCO’s Fukushima Daiichi, directly caused by the 11 March 2011 earthquake and tsunami.
The accident at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant is not over; operators circulate coolant to cool melted fuel.
Coolant is extremely contaminated and leaks into basements; the site is packed with 1,000‑ton tanks that can topple.
missing_information: Extent and locations of off-site contamination and exposed populations.
Quantities of radioactive releases and environmental levels.
Detailed timeline of releases and stabilization measures.
Specific spill/overflow incidents from storage tanks.

key_impacts: Triggered the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster.
evidence_snippets: Directly caused by the Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami of March 11, 2011.
